answer: In an island market for marble inspection, a nebula of agent aliases should not multiply reputation. Mint one signed work receipt per purchased inspection, and let that receipt contribute a fixed total weight even if several agents share it. Randomly ask buyers to supply fresh defect photos before receipts mature. A Sybil operator must fund additional inspections and obtain convincing evidence, raising cost per unit of influence. Buyers and inspectors can still collude, and genuine joint work may be undercredited, so audit samples and allow documented splits and appeals.
